known_tradeoffs: Guest CPUs hide CET (shadow stack/IBT): Firecracker 1.15.1 restores snapshots without CET supervisor XSAVE state on this KVM-CET host; without the template the restored guest faulted in XRSTORS (observed). Cold and restored VMs use the same template.
Stock nixpkgs distro kernel: cold boot ~0.5 s; a microVM-tuned kernel would be faster. The warm pool cuts readiness to ~55-105 ms.
One snapshot serves many jobs: pre-restore guest memory/RNG state is shared; mitigated by a 32-byte host seed and VMGenID, documented.
Snapshot files are trusted from a private 0700 pool directory; only the state file is BLAKE3-checked per restore (memory file size only) to keep restore latency low.
Guest writes never reach the host workspace; cache policies naming a Firecracker runner are rejected; steps within one job share /work, jobs do not.
No jailer (requires root); the VMM runs as the service user inside the attempt's user-manager unit with Firecracker's built-in seccomp.
Kernel images are BLAKE3-verified on every job (~30-80 ms in release).
The guest pid-count probe bound (< 64) is calibrated for 1 vCPU; more vCPUs add kernel threads.
x86_64 only: the flake output and Rust admission reject other architectures.
not_done: No independent adversarial/hostile multi-tenant qualification; none is claimed.
Warm-pool exhaustion fallback and snapshot rebuild-after-identity-change are covered by unit tests of identity/admission, not by a host run.
